A precondition for a transfer of information to a person or another new physical carrier is the presence of the respective information object and this person or physical thing in one event.

Examples of the inverse property:
- Deckchair 42 (E19) was present at the sinking of the Titanic (E5). (Aldridge, 2008)

In First Order Logic of the inverse property:
- P12(x,y) ⇒ E5(x)
- P12(x,y) ⇒ E77(y)

terms.label: was produced by
terms.definition:
Quantification of the inverse property: one to many, necessary, dependent (1,n:1,1)

Scope note of the inverse property:
This property identifies the instance of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing that came into existence as a result of the instance of E12 Production.
The identity of an instance of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing is not defined by its matter, but by its existence as a subject of documentation. An E12 Production can result in the creation of multiple instances of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing.

Examples of the inverse property:
- The building of Rome (E12) has produced the Colosseum (E24). (Hopkins & Beard, 2011)

In First Order Logic of the inverse property:
- P108(x,y) ⇒ E12(x)
- P108(x,y) ⇒ E24(y)
- P108(x,y) ⇒ P31(x,y)
- P108(x,y) ⇒ P92(x,y)

terms.label: wasAssociatedWith
terms.definition: An prov:Agent that had some (unspecified) responsibility for the occurrence of this prov:Activity.

terms.label: wasAttributedTo
terms.definition: Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.

terms.label: wasDerivedFrom
terms.definition: A derivation is a transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity.

terms.label: wasInfluencedBy
terms.definition: Because prov:wasInfluencedBy is a broad relation, its more specific subproperties (e.g. prov:wasInformedBy, prov:actedOnBehalfOf, prov:wasEndedBy, etc.) should be used when applicable.

terms.label: wasInformedBy
terms.definition: An activity a2 is dependent on or informed by another activity a1, by way of some unspecified entity that is generated by a1 and used by a2.

terms.label: wasRevisionOf
terms.definition: A revision is a derivation that revises an entity into a revised version.

terms.label: Confidence score
terms.definition: Degree of belief, between 0 and 1, that the asserted value is correct: 1 = certain, 0.5 = undecided, 0 = believed false. The assessor is either the agent the assertion is attributed to (prov:wasAttributedTo) or the activity that generated the assertion (prov:wasGeneratedBy), e.g. an extraction that codes how firmly the source states the claim; hg:confidenceMethod says which, and by what rubric. Scores are comparable only when they share an assessor or a method.

terms.label: Custodian type
terms.definition: Type of custodian (government, academic, community), free text.

terms.label: Data quality note
terms.definition: Notes on data quality, completeness, or uncertainty.

terms.label: Datacite identifier
terms.definition: Persistent identifier for the source (DOI, archive ID, catalog number).

terms.label: Datacite identifier type
terms.definition: Type of identifier (DOI, ISBN, Handle, LocalArchiveID).

terms.label: Datacite resource type
terms.definition: High-level DataCite resource type (Dataset, Text, Image, Audio, Interview).

terms.label: endedAtTime
terms.definition: The time at which an activity ended. See also prov:startedAtTime.

terms.label: Epoch date gregorian
terms.definition: Proleptic Gregorian (ISO 8601, astronomical year numbering) date on which the era began, in the era's own reckoning (Bikram Sambat counts from year 1, e.g. -0056-04-14, a nominal back-projection of the modern solar reckoning rather than an attested date; Nepal Sambat counts elapsed years from year 0, 0879-10-24 = 20 October 879 Julian). Its month and day only indicate the approximate new-year season: the actual new year varies (Bikram Sambat 13-15 April, solar; Nepal Sambat late October to November, lunisolar), so it must not be used for day-level conversion. A value ending in -01-01 marks a calendar whose new year is 1 January, for which year conversion is exact.

terms.label: Expertise area
terms.definition: Areas of expertise (e.g., Licchavi inscriptions, Sanskrit epigraphy, Newari archaeology).

terms.label: generatedAtTime
terms.definition: The time at which an entity was completely created and is available for use.

terms.label: has note
terms.definition:
Quantification: one to many (0,n:0,1)

Scope note:
This property is a container for all informal descriptions about an object that have not been expressed in terms of CIDOC CRM constructs. 
In particular, it captures the characterisation of the item itself, its internal structures, appearance, etc.
Like property P2 has type (is type of), this property is a consequence of the restricted focus of the CIDOC CRM. The aim is not to capture, in a structured form, everything that can be said about an item; indeed, the CIDOC CRM formalism is not regarded as sufficient to express everything that can be said. Good practice requires use of distinct note fields for different aspects of a characterisation. The P3.1 has type property of P3 has note allows differentiation of specific notes, e.g. “construction”, “decoration”, etc. 
An item may have many notes, but a note is attached to a specific item.

Examples:
- Coffee mug – OXCMS:1983.1.1 (E19) has note “chipped at edge of handle” (E62) has type Condition (E55). (fictitious)

Properties:
- P3.1 has type: E55 Type

In First Order Logic:
- P3(x,y) ⇒ E1(x)
- P3(x,y) ⇒ E62(y) 
- P3(x,y,z) ⇒ [P3(x,y) ∧ E55(z)]

terms.label: Identifier
terms.definition: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.

terms.label: inLanguage
terms.definition: The language of the content or performance or used in an action. Please use one of the language codes from the [IETF BCP 47 standard](http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47). See also [[availableLanguage]].

terms.label: Institutional affiliation
terms.definition: Institutional affiliation (e.g., Tribhuvan University, Nepal Heritage Society).

terms.label: Is critical for festival
terms.definition: Whether this ritual is essential for the festival's completion.

terms.label: Last known existence date
terms.definition: Latest date when this structure is documented as existing (ISO 8601).

terms.label: Lunar date tithi
terms.definition: Lunar day (tithi) by which the practice is timed, in free text (e.g. 'Bhadra Shukla Chaturdashi').

terms.label: obsolete curator
terms.definition: Person or organization curating the dataset.

terms.label: obsolete dataset name
terms.definition: Human-readable name of the dataset.

terms.label: obsolete dataset version
terms.definition: Version identifier of the dataset instance.

terms.label: obsolete generated date
terms.definition: Date the dataset serialization was generated (ISO 8601).

terms.label: obsolete license
terms.definition: License under which the dataset is released.

terms.label: obsolete schema version
terms.definition: HeritageGraph schema version the dataset conforms to.

terms.label: obsolete selection criteria met
terms.definition: DEPRECATED free-text list; use hg:hasCriterion -> SelectionCriterion subclasses instead. Retained for backward compatibility.

terms.label: place is defined by
terms.definition:
Quantification: one to many, dependent (0,n:1,1)

Scope note:
This property associates an instance of E53 Place with an instance of E94 Space Primitive that defines it. Syntactic variants or use of different scripts may result in multiple instances of E94 Space Primitive defining exactly the same place. Transformations between different reference systems always result in new definitions of places approximating each other and not in alternative definitions.

Examples:
- The centroid from https://sws.geonames.org/735927 (E53) place is defined by 40°31'17.9"N 21°15'48.3"E (E94). [A single point for approximating the centre of the city of Kastoria, Greece]
- Martin’s coordinates for Kastoria (E53) place is defined by 40°30'23"N 21°14'53"E, 40°31'40"N 21°16'43"E (E94). [A square covering the built settlement structure of Kastoria, Greece]
- Martin’s centroid for Kastoria (E53) place is defined by 40°31'01.5"N 21°15'48"E (E94). [A point in the lake of Kastoria in the centre of the area covered by the city]
- The position measured by Alexander von Humboldt for the Plaza Mayor in Cumaná, Sucre, Venezuela 1799-1800AD (E53) place is defined by 10°27'52"N 66°30'02"W (E94). [West of the Observatory of Paris = 64°09'51"W of Greenwich, actually 1.1km east of today’s Plaza Andrés Eloy Blanco of Cumaná] (Humboldt, 1859)

In First Order Logic:
- P168(x,y) ⇒ E53(x)
- P168(x,y) ⇒ E94(y)

terms.label: Place type
terms.definition: Type of place (city, village, region), free text.

terms.label: Proposition object literal
terms.definition: Object of the proposition when it is a literal value (e.g. a date).

terms.label: Proposition predicate
terms.definition: Property (URI/CURIE) claimed of the subject, e.g. crm:P108i_was_produced_by (plays the role of rdf:predicate).

terms.label: Reconciliation status
terms.definition: Status of multi-source reconciliation of the asserted value: confirmed (independent sources agree), conflicting (sources disagree; see the competing assertions), or unverified (single source, not yet checked).

terms.label: Recorded date
terms.definition: The date as written in the source, in the calendar given by hg:calendarSystem (e.g. '2072' for a Bikram Sambat year, 'NS 1135 Kaulaathwa', 'VS 2021'). It is never put into an xsd:dateTime: the converted Gregorian bounds go in crm:P82a_begin_of_the_begin / crm:P82b_end_of_the_end.

terms.label: Recurrence pattern
terms.definition: How the practice this occurrence belongs to recurs (e.g. annual, monthly), in free text. It describes the practice, not the occurrence: each occurrence is its own RitualEvent with its own time-span.

terms.label: Role duty
terms.definition: The ritual duty held (e.g. building the festival chariot, performing the daily worship).

terms.label: Route description
terms.definition: Text description of the procession route.

terms.label: Source citation
terms.definition: Formal citation of source.

terms.label: Source url
terms.definition: URL or digital identifier for source.

terms.label: startedAtTime
terms.definition: The time at which an activity started. See also prov:endedAtTime.

terms.label: Succession rule
terms.definition: Rule by which the duty passes on (e.g. eldest son of the lineage; within the caste group).

terms.label: Traditional role
terms.definition: Hereditary occupation or ritual duty.

terms.label: Used equipment
terms.definition: Equipment used in documentation.

terms.label: Used method
terms.definition: Documentation method used.

terms.label: value
terms.definition: Provides a value that is a direct representation of an entity.

terms.label: Verification method
terms.definition: Method used for verification (cross-check, expert review, field visit).

terms.label: Year offset from gregorian
terms.definition: Number of years this calendar runs ahead of the Gregorian (Common Era) year at the start of its year (e.g. 57 for Bikram Sambat, -879 for Nepal Sambat). Because the calendar's new year does not fall on 1 January (see hg:epochDateGregorian), a year-precision date Y converts to the two-year interval [Y - offset, Y - offset + 1] CE; the single year Y - offset is correct only for dates between the calendar's new year and 31 December. A calendar whose new year is 1 January converts to Y - offset exactly.

terms.label: obsolete crminf pattern
terms.definition: Editorial note naming the CRMinf pattern that a class instantiates.

terms.label: obsolete design note
terms.definition: Editorial note recording a modelling decision about a term.

terms.label: obsolete prov alignment
terms.definition: Editorial note naming the PROV-O term that a slot is aligned with.

terms.label: obsolete prov alignment note
terms.definition: Editorial note explaining the status of a class's PROV-O alignment.

terms.label: obsolete provenance scope
terms.definition: States whether a class's provenance slots describe the data record or the real-world referent.

terms.label: Access Protocol (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Cultural access protocol for heritage knowledge or a record of it, to be set with the community concerned.

terms.label: Architectural Style (concept scheme)
terms.definition: A vocabulary of architectural styles for South Asian heritage, mapped to CIDOC E55 Type.

terms.label: Condition Type (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary for the physical condition of heritage objects and structures.

terms.label: Date Precision (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary for the temporal precision of recorded heritage dates.

terms.label: Endowment Event Type (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary for events in the life of a Guthi endowment.

terms.label: Existence Status (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary for whether a heritage structure still exists physically.

terms.label: Guthi Type (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary of Guthi functional types (CRM E55_Type).

terms.label: HeritageGraph LinkML schema
terms.definition: The LinkML schema from which this ontology is generated; every generated term is skos:inScheme it.

terms.label: Ritual Type (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary of ritual and festival activity types in Kathmandu Valley living heritage.

terms.label: Syncretic Type (concept scheme)
terms.definition: Controlled vocabulary for kinds of syncretic theological relationships between deities.

terms.label: Abhisheka
terms.definition: Ritual bathing/anointing of deity.

terms.label: Alienation of an endowment
terms.definition: Loss of endowed property to private or other ownership (sale, encroachment, registration in a private name).

terms.label: Appropriation
terms.definition: Claimed adoption: one tradition is held to have taken the deity over from the other.

terms.label: Augmentation of an endowment
terms.definition: Addition of land or other property to an existing endowment.

terms.label: Bhajan
terms.definition: Devotional singing ritual.

terms.label: Century
terms.definition: Within century range.

terms.label: Chariot Procession
terms.definition: Ritual chariot pulling.

terms.label: Circa
terms.definition: Approximate date.

terms.label: Circumambulation
terms.definition: Ritual circular movement around sacred site.

terms.label: Community Use Only
terms.definition: For use within the community concerned; not for general publication.

terms.label: Damaged
terms.definition: Partially damaged.

terms.label: Decade
terms.definition: Within 10-year range.

terms.label: Deinstallation Ritual
terms.definition: De-installation/conclusion ritual.

terms.label: Deity guthi
terms.definition: Deity guthi (dyah guthi): an association, usually endowed with land, that keeps up the worship and the festival of a deity at its temple or shrine.

terms.label: Destroyed
terms.definition: Known to have been destroyed; no physical remains.

terms.label: Dome style
terms.definition: Dome-based style (Mughal/Neo-classical influence).

terms.label: Equivalence
terms.definition: Claimed identity: the two are held to be one deity in different traditions (e.g. Avalokiteshvara and Matsyendranath for Newar Buddhists).

terms.label: Exact
terms.definition: Precise date known.

terms.label: Extant
terms.definition: Currently exists in physical form.

terms.label: Founding of an endowment
terms.definition: Dedication of land or other property that creates an endowment (and usually its Guthi).

terms.label: Fusion
terms.definition: Claimed combination: the deity is held to combine features of deities of several traditions.

terms.label: Good
terms.definition: No significant damage.

terms.label: Historical
terms.definition: Claimed historical derivation: the deity is held to have developed from the other over time.

terms.label: Homa
terms.definition: Fire offering ritual.

terms.label: Hypothetical
terms.definition: Theorized (e.g. a reconstruction on paper only); never physically realized.

terms.label: Initiates Only
terms.definition: Restricted to initiates (e.g. the agam deity and rites of a lineage or monastery).

terms.label: Installation Ritual
terms.definition: Installation/enshrinement ritual.

terms.label: Jatra
terms.definition: Festival procession ritual.

terms.label: Jatra Guthi
terms.definition: Festival organization trust.

terms.label: Kamya Puja
terms.definition: Desire-based optional worship.

terms.label: Lost
terms.definition: Existence documented but location/remains unknown.

terms.label: Masked Performance
terms.definition: Ritual masked dance.

terms.label: Month
terms.definition: Month-level precision (e.g. a lunar month of a given year).

terms.label: Naimittika Puja
terms.definition: Occasional/Festival worship.

terms.label: Nasha Guthi
terms.definition: Music and dance trust.

terms.label: Nationalisation of an endowment
terms.definition: Transfer of an endowment to state administration (e.g. the Guthi Sansthan, established 1964 CE / VS 2021).

terms.label: Nitya Puja
terms.definition: Daily mandatory worship.

terms.label: obsolete Chaitya style
terms.definition: Buddhist votive shrine style.

terms.label: obsolete San Guthi
terms.definition: Variant spelling of sanah guthi.

terms.label: obsolete Stupa style
terms.definition: Buddhist dome-shaped reliquary.

terms.label: Open
terms.definition: No community restriction on access or publication.

terms.label: Pagoda style
terms.definition: Multi-tiered roof form of the Kathmandu Valley, as in the Newar tiered temple: roofs that diminish upward and rest on carved struts (also used on other building types).

terms.label: Partially Extant
terms.definition: Fragments or ruins remain.

terms.label: Procession Ritual
terms.definition: Ritual procession/movement.

terms.label: Processional Movement
terms.definition: General ritual movement between locations.

terms.label: Puja Guthi
terms.definition: Daily worship trust.

terms.label: Raj Guthi
terms.definition: Royal endowment trust.

terms.label: Reconstructed
terms.definition: Destroyed or collapsed and rebuilt: it exists again in physical form, with a documented reconstruction (record the reconstruction as an event, e.g. crm:E11_Modification).

terms.label: Relic Tour
terms.definition: Procession with sacred relics between sites.

terms.label: Restored
terms.definition: Repaired and stabilized.

terms.label: Returning Ritual
terms.definition: Return to normal state ritual.

terms.label: Ritual Consecration
terms.definition: Consecration/activation ritual.

terms.label: Ruined
terms.definition: Severely damaged or collapsed.

terms.label: Sana Guthi
terms.definition: Funeral association (sanah guthi): the association that organises the funeral procession and cremation of member households; in some localities it and the si guthi are one body.

terms.label: Seasonal
terms.definition: Access or use only at certain times (e.g. during a festival).

terms.label: Secret Sacred
terms.definition: Secret or sacred knowledge with specific conditions of access.

terms.label: Shikhara style
terms.definition: North Indian spire-shaped style.

terms.label: Si Guthi
terms.definition: Death guthi (si guthi): the association whose members carry out the cremation and death rites of member households.

terms.label: Unknown
terms.definition: Existence status uncertain.

terms.label: Vrata
terms.definition: Vow observance ritual.

terms.label: Yagna
terms.definition: Vedic sacrifice ritual.

terms.label: Year
terms.definition: Year-level precision only.
